acceptance: Decision gate: the owner confirms that release/* maintenance branches count as integration branches for worktree finish and reap. The recommended rule is a pattern, release/<major>.<minor>.x, not a literal list, so new lines need no code change. The decision is recorded here before any edit.

worktree-finish and worktree-reap give a 'remove' verdict to a clean worktree whose HEAD is exactly the merged head of a PR into release/0.5.x, using the same proofs as for develop (merged head, clean, nothing unpushed, managed provenance). Unit tests cover a release/<x>.x base being accepted and an arbitrary non-integration base (for example a feature branch) still being held.
A dry run of make worktree-reap no longer classes the three worktrees above as ambiguous because of their base, or each has already been removed by its owning session.

Guardrails: no other safety condition is relaxed (dirty, unpushed, detached, open PR, locked, current worktree and primary clone are still kept); the remote branch is never deleted; worktrees owned by a live session are not removed by hand while testing; the release-line machinery other sessions are building is not edited, only the base check.
description: STRUCTURAL_BASES in _project/scripts/worktree_audit.py is {develop, release, published-results}, and scripts/worktree_finish.py holds any worktree whose merged PR targets another base with hold_code non_structural_base. Maintenance-line work now merges into release/0.5.x (docs/internal/release-guide.md describes release/* lines, and trunk.yml and the review policy already cover release/**). On 2026-11-17 a make worktree-reap dry run classed three clean worktrees as ambiguous for this reason alone: BenchBox.wt-line-noop (PR #4249), BenchBox.wt-release-0.5.2rc1 (PR #4250) and BenchBox.wt-line-starrocks-rc2 (PR #4303), all merged into release/0.5.x. Every future maintenance-line worktree will pile up the same way and need removing by hand.
